paperTitle: Perceptions of Voice Interaction in Digital Games: A Comparative Study
centralContribution: This study investigates and comparatively analyzes perceptions of voice interaction in digital games across three core scenarios (game-to-player, player-to-player, player-to-game) among game experts, undergraduate students, and generative AIs, aiming to provide insights for improving gameplay experiences, reducing disruptive behaviors, and identifying opportunities for health and wellness applications.

gameObjects.visualMetaphor: The study's central contribution is a comparative analysis of perceptions regarding voice interaction in digital games, involving human experts, students, and generative AIs across three interaction scenarios (game-to-player, player-to-player, player-to-game). The aim is to enhance gameplay, mitigate disruptive behaviors, and explore applications in health and wellness.

Voice interaction, despite its ubiquity in daily life, faces fluctuating integration in digital games due to technical limitations (e.g., microphone quality, transcription inaccuracies, ambient noise) and socio-behavioral issues (e.g., toxic player conduct, identity dissonance). This challenge is particularly acute in health-related games where voice interaction is scarce despite its potential for accessibility and rehabilitation. The paper addresses this by conducting a comparative study to understand diverse perceptions of voice interaction, leveraging advancements in AI and voice recognition to guide future game development, especially for enhancing immersion, engagement, and health applications.
